# The comment dedup key is NOT normalized the way the description send value is

## Summary

The description path and the comment path have different convergence protections, and the missing
piece is exactly the normalization half. Today this is LATENT — it costs nothing, because rebar does
not currently model any content transformation on the comment send path. Any real Markdown/wiki
converter activates it, and the symptom is duplicate Jira comments re-posted on every pass, forever.

Filed from a peer session's round-trip experiment over 5,568 real rebar bodies, verified here
against the code rather than taken on report.

## The asymmetry, in code

**Descriptions are protected.** `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.map_fields_to_remote` composes

    normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))

so the value sent is already its own fixed point under the round trip. The ordering is deliberate and
documented in a long comment there, and it is PINNED by
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_seam_heldout.py::test_cloud_send_path_composition_is_unchanged`,
which includes an explicitly soft-wrapped case.

**Comments are not.** `outbound_comments._diff_comments` builds its comparison key with

    compare_body = sanitizer.fit_comment(_normalize_comment_body(raw))

There is no `normalize_outbound` equivalent. And `_normalize_comment_body` does NOT normalize both
sides the same way — it calls `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`, which is:

    if isinstance(body, dict):  return adf_to_text(body)     # the JIRA side: decoded
    return str(body) if body is not None else ""             # the LOCAL side: pass-through

So the Jira side is decoded and the local side is handed back verbatim. The two sides are compared
after DIFFERENT transformations.

## Why the truncation guard proves the shape of the bug

The comment path already carries one guard of exactly this kind, added after it bit:

> the send path truncates an over-length body ... Apply the SAME shared truncation to the expected
> local body before the membership test; otherwise the full local body never matches the truncated
> Jira body and the diff re-emits forever.

That is the identical failure mode, patched for the ONE transformation the send path was known to
apply. Nothing generalizes it. A content transformation gets no such treatment, and the machinery
that would notice — a comparison against what Jira will actually store — does not exist.

The `_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES` canary exclusion is a second instance of the same class patched
per-symptom: a volatile timestamp never matches a prior body, so the comment re-added every pass.

## Why it is latent RIGHT NOW (do not "fix" a bug that is not firing)

Cloud comments go out through ACLI as `jira workitem comment create --body <text>`
(`acli_cli_ops.add_comment`). rebar never computes the ADF that Jira will store, so it applies no
content transformation of its own, and the dedup key happens to match. DC's `WikiTextCodec` is pure
identity in all four operations, so DC transforms nothing either.

I could not establish whether ACLI's own text→ADF conversion alters bodies (e.g. rejoining soft
wraps) — that is a live question about a third-party binary and only a live pass settles it. If it
DOES, this is already firing on Cloud today. Empirically, rebar's own `text_to_adf` DOES rejoin soft
wraps, so the transformation is not hypothetical for that encoder.

## What I verified empirically (so the future work is not built on a wrong premise)

Probing today's `adf.normalize_description` directly: `**/*.py`, `__pycache__`, `**a** **b**`, pipe
tables, backticks, fenced blocks, `-`/`*` bullets and `__bold__` all round-trip BYTE-IDENTICALLY and
are fixed points. Today's ADF path does no Markdown parsing at all — it only rejoins soft wraps and
strips trailing whitespace. So the peer session's 9-19% flap rate is a property of the PROPOSED
converter, not of anything shipping.

## The good news: the seam is already in the right place

`map_fields_to_remote` is SHARED and composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(...))` for both
backends, so a pandoc-backed `WikiTextCodec` slots in by implementing the codec — no differ change.
The `RichTextCodec` four-operation split is what makes that possible. This ticket is about the
comment path catching up to the description path, not about redesigning the seam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the comment dedup key is computed from what the SEND PATH will produce, the same way the
      description value is — i.e. the local comparison key goes through the codec's outbound
      normalization, not just `fit_comment`
- [x] a test asserts the property directly: given a codec whose outbound transform is NOT the
      identity, a local comment already mirrored in Jira emits NO add. This is the cell that does
      not exist today — every current dedup test uses transformations applied to both sides
- [x] a corpus/property test over real rebar comment bodies asserts encode-then-decode is a fixed
      point for the comment path, not just unit examples
- [x] `RichTextCodec` implementations are pinned to `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`.
      `WikiTextCodec`'s identity satisfies this trivially TODAY, which is why a pandoc implementation
      that got it wrong would pass the existing suite
- [x] the dependency is DOCUMENTED: outbound has no origin-aware gate, and the reason it does not
      need one is that degradation is symmetric. If encode ever stops being decode's inverse, a body
      pulled from Jira starts being re-emitted and the human's Jira-native formatting is destroyed.
      That invariant is currently load-bearing and unwritten
